summary: MSVC CRT file-close internals. When the state flags at a1+0xC have any of bits 0x83 set (file open/writeable state), it flushes buffered writes via BufferFlushWrite, releases the stream lock via sub_58C411, closes the OS file handle at a1+0x10 through sub_58C331, and on success frees the heap-allocated buffer pointer stored at a1+0x1C via sub_58AA6F, clearing it to 0. On failure the default -1 is returned. The state flags at a1+0xC are unconditionally reset to 0 before returning.

local_names.v1: close result: the OS close status, or -1 on failure

operations.description: Initialize v1 to -1 as the default close result.
Guard on the file state at a1+0xC: (flags & 0x83) != 0 selects the open-file close path.
BufferFlushWrite(a1) flushes any buffered writes to the OS before the handle is closed.
sub_58C411(a1) releases the stream lock held on the file object.
Guard on the OS handle at a1+0x10: sub_58C331(handle) must return >= 0 for the close to succeed; otherwise v1 stays -1.
sub_58AA6F(a1+0x1C) frees the heap-allocated internal buffer when the pointer is non-zero.
Clear the buffer pointer at a1+0x1C to 0 after freeing it.
Reset the file state flags at a1+0xC to 0 unconditionally before returning.
Return v1: the OS close result, or -1 when the file was not in an open state or the close failed.
Invoked by the locked close wrapper FileCloseWithLock.

unresolved: The exact meaning of each flag bit in 0x83 at a1+0xC is not decomposed here beyond 'open/writeable state'.
The object type of the file stream is unknown; offsets 0xC, 0x10 and 0x1C are treated as state, OS handle and buffer pointer respectively.
